description: Golden fixtures for the Runbook Executor. The eval path runs with skip_approval=True (no approver), so destructive steps deterministically resolve to 'denied' at the HITL gate while non-destructive steps execute autonomously. Cases assert selection + the resolution status + step accounting, not exact LLM strings (RA-004 uses no LLM). Retargeted from the OTel Demo services (payment/cart/checkout) to the ecommerce SUT when those runbooks were deleted in the migration.

cases.description: A payment-service incident with no specific fault tag selects the generic restart runbook; the safe drain step runs, the destructive restart is gated -> denied.
'paymentservice' normalizes to the same service as 'payment-service' and still selects the runbook.
An OOM incident selects the memory-leak runbook over the generic restart, because tag overlap outscores a service-only match. Its clear_fault step is destructive, so it is gated.
A database dependency outage selects the MySQL runbook, which clears the fault, waits on the datastore, then verifies the app.
A service with no matching runbook returns a clean 'no_runbook' outcome rather than guessing.
